change.summary: GET /{event-id} stopped returning twelve edges (attending, comments, declined, feed, interested, live_videos, maybe, noreply, photos, pictures, posts, videos), and every app — including already-approved ones — was required to pass App Review to regain access. Filed by Meta as a non-versioned change, defined on their own page as taking effect immediately across all API versions, so pinning v2.5 through v2.12 gave no protection.

spec.note: Meta has never published an OpenAPI document for the general Graph API. The only Meta-owned Swagger artifact found was facebookarchive/Facebook-Server-Side-API-Swagger, created 2020-02-11 — 22 months later, now archived, and scoped to the Conversions advertiser API rather than the Event node.

changelog.note: Announced and enforced the same day, so the changelog was a notification of an outage rather than a warning. This is the case that shows announced_at alone is not the metric: detection was perfect and the lead time was zero.

contract.note: Silent in the HTTP sense — the edges returned empty arrays rather than 4xx, so it read as 'this event has no posts' and was hard to attribute. An error-rate monitor sees nothing; a monitor recording that an edge that always returned items now returns none catches it.

notes: Widely misattributed to Graph API v3.0, which shipped a month later on 2018-05-01; it was a non-versioned change. Meta paused App Review at the same time, so the documented remediation was unavailable for weeks — the maintainer's thread runs April to July with users stranded. No amount of monitoring helps here: with zero notice, the best any tool can do is tell you the same day, which is what contract verification would have done.
